Turyysk Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Turyysk (Trisk in Yiddish) is first mentioned as home to Jews in the mid-16th century; the Maggid of Trisk, Avraham Twersky (1806–1889) — son of Mordechai Twersky of Chernobyl, documented elsewhere in this collection — created a Hasidic court here and built a synagogue for his followers. In the late 18th century, the Maskilic physician Dr. Moses Marcuse practiced in Turyysk, publishing 'Sefer HaRefuot' (Book of Cures), the first medical book ever published in Yiddish. The Jewish population reached 1,713 (58.4 percent) by 1897. Following the June 1941 occupation, a ghetto was liquidated on August 10, 1942, with around 1,512 Jews shot near this very cemetery. This cemetery, established between the 16th and 17th centuries, was shut down in the late 19th century, mostly holding wooden gravestones now long gone; in 2013, Israel Meir Gabbai fenced the site, including the ohel of the Trisker Maggid, who is buried here alongside his wife and daughter, along with the grave of the daughter of Yom-Tov Lipmann Heller (author of Tosafot Yom Tov), documented elsewhere in this collection, whose husband served as rabbi of Volodymyr-Volynsky.
